research.title: UK government reverses course, abandons plan to let AI companies train on copyrighted music without permission
research.summary: UK Technology Secretary Liz Kendall announces government 'no longer has a preferred option' on AI copyright reform, reversing from earlier stance that would have allowed AI devs to train on copyrighted works unless rightsholders opted out. Major win for music industry and creative sector lobbying. Government will now pursue broader consultation rather than mandated exception.

research.title: Sony Music targets 135,000+ deepfakes of its artists' music for removal from streaming platforms
research.summary: Sony Music has asked streaming platforms to remove 135,000+ deepfake tracks impersonating its artists, including Beyoncé, Queen, and Harry Styles. Sony says this is likely only a fraction of the actual total. Dennis Kooker (Sony President, Global Digital) notes deepfakes cause 'direct commercial harm' and are 'demand-driven events' exploiting artist promotion cycles. Company flagged ~60,000 in the past year alone, up from 75,000 the prior year.

research.title: Streaming fraud man who pocketed $8M using hundreds of thousands of AI songs streamed billions of times pleads guilty
research.summary: Michael Smith of Cornelius, NC pleads guilty to one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud in first-ever US criminal prosecution for AI-assisted streaming fraud. Smith used AI to generate thousands of fake songs, streamed them billions of times via bots, and diverted $8M in royalties from real artists. Facing up to 5 years prison (reduced from 60 years under initial charges). Must forfeit $8M+. Sentencing July 29.

research.summary: BMG files lawsuit against Anthropic claiming the AI company's massive $380B valuation was built on copyrighted works used without license - a major escalation of copyright wars beyond the music industry into AI company valuation itself.
